name: Captain Heathyr

facts.text: Heathyr's blows bleed for 65 every 3 seconds for 30 seconds.
Every named of the Hall takes no damage once drawn past its tether, and walks back to its post.

story:
The door. Captain Heathyr kept the door of the captains' hall, the last gate between the upper hall and the road, and she had it rehung the season before the corruption came, because she liked a door that shut properly. On the last night, the clerk wrote, she was at the door when the wizard came down, and she said that she could not feel her hands. Like every officer of the Pennine watch, it is bound to its post: one step past where its captain stood it, no blow lands and it walks home at full health. Fight it where it stands. 

She held the door anyway, while the other captains sat down at the table and did not get up again. She was the last of the three to fall, and her post is the doorway still. Her blows bleed like her brothers', and she fights as if the door at her back still mattered, which, to the dead watch, it does: behind it sit Atwell and Bardalph and the clerk with his pen. The hall's dead do not know that the war they kept the door for ended long ago. Heathyr, the bards say, suspects it, and holds the door anyway.

The riders from Camelot who found the watch could have passed her, the bards say; she was only one dead captain in a doorway. They did not. Something in the way she turned her head told them the door was still held, and they went back down the hall the way they had come, and that is why the order to seal the road was never carried out.
legend: Same as the other captains: her blows bleed for half a minute, so the tank needs steady heals from the first swing. Fight her in the doorway where she stands; she will not leave it and cannot be hurt a step beyond it. She is the last of the three captains, and the strongest-willed: the old hands kill her last, after Atwell and Bardalph, so that only one bleeding captain is ever on the raid at a time. She fights behind a shield and answers a block with a hard return blow, so her exchanges run long. Heathyr does not chase; she holds. Use that, and pull her a single step into the room.

aggro: I cannot feel my hands. I do not need them.

lairEntry: A captain in the doorway. She has not moved in years.
The door was rehung. It shuts properly.

loremasterTopic.text: Captain Heathyr kept the gate of the captains' hall and was the last of the three captains to fall, holding the door while the others sat down at the table and did not get up again.

bookPage: Then Captain Heathyr, at the door, said that she could not feel her hands, and Captain Bardalph said that he had told us so, and the Lady Darra began to pray. That is the last thing the clerk Tobias wrote. The riders from Camelot found Heathyr in the doorway of the captains' hall, standing, her sword in hands that had gone the colour of slate. She turned her head when they came in. They did not try to pass her. They went back the way they had come, and the riders' captain said afterwards that it was the first time in his life he had been turned back by a door.
